profiles.review_note:
Independent EA-PDF rule review: clauses 1–7 and Tables 1–7
Date: 2026-10-31
Source: docs/reference/EA-PDF-v1.pdf, February 2025 edition, printed pp1–58; cross-read §9.1–9.6 pp61–70 for normative counterparts and Tables 6–7.
Compared: current validator_rule_text.json (213 entries), not an earlier rule snapshot.
Scope: read-only specification/extraction review. No conversion, code edits, or execution tests. Current view-only requirements registry consulted only after direct reading to distinguish existing recorded questions from new wording findings.

Main conclusion
The early descriptive material is substantially accounted for, and several previous over-strict interpretations have already been repaired. The remaining work is chiefly (a) keeping exact source assertions in the executable rule catalogue, (b) retaining exceptions and strength separately from implementation policy, and (c) visibly recording disagreements within the published specification. Do not automatically translate every descriptive 'must' or example into a new PDF-only failure.

Confirmed wording/traceability gaps
1. Source coverage and header fidelity are bundled, but only one survives in the text.
Rules: MESSAGE_SOURCE_MATCH #8.
Source: §7.2 printed p35; §7.3.1 printed p36.
Current rule links both SOURCE-COVERAGE and HEADER-SOURCE-EQUIVALENCE, yet its spec_excerpt only says embedded source data covers represented emails. Section 7.3.1 separately says document XMP must reflect full source header values as equivalently as possible subject to encoding differences. Visible labels may be localized; stored XMP semantics must not be translated or shortened merely to fit a page. Restore this distinct creator/source-dependent assertion. A PDF-only comparison cannot prove it without independent input evidence.
Severity: medium extraction gap; high confidence. No runtime bug claim.

2. The attachment rule loses its precise page-boundary condition.
Rule: ATTACHMENT_ANNOTATIONS_PRESENT #59.
Source: §7.5 pp43–45, normative §9.3 printed p65.
Current rule says a visible FileAttachment annotation is needed within each relevant BodyRendering Content Set, then spends most of its text explaining identity/evidence policy. The normative assertion also requires the annotation to be positioned entirely inside the page CropBox, with MediaBox fallback. Being somewhere on the appropriate page is insufficient. Restore this exact condition as a separate check and keep association uncertainty policy separate.
Severity: medium extraction gap; high confidence. Code enforcement not audited here.

3. The embedded-media rules do not fully state the PDF object requirements.
Rules: EMBEDDED_SUBTYPE_MATCH_XMP #68; SOURCE_MEDIATYPE_PARAMETERS_MATCH #69; EMBEDDED_MEDIATYPE_RECONSTRUCTION #70.
Source: §7.1.3 p33; §7.5 p46; normative §9.4 p66–67.
The current excerpts focus on association, matching, and reconstruction. The original separately requires every embedded-file stream to carry Subtype as its bare IANA type, without semicolons or parameters, and the separate Mail_MediaTypeParameters value is a PDF string when source parameters exist. These object presence/type/syntax assertions should be explicit, not inferred from a broad comparison description. #70 already labels its semicolon deviation as a local interpretation; preserve that label.
Severity: medium extraction gap; high confidence. Shared with the §9 reviewer; avoid duplicate finding.

Current specification questions, already partly tracked elsewhere
4. PDF/A profile matrix and edition must not be silently flattened or promoted.
Rules: PDFA_PART #3; PDFA_CONFORMANCE #4.
Source: §3.2 Table2 pp8–11; §4 p15; §7.1.3 p32; normative §9.1 p61.
Table2 lists plain PDF/A-4 only for isolated si/mi, and lists c/ci only against 3a/3u/4f. It prints the invalid designation '4fe' for m. However §3 expressly calls itself descriptive, while normative §9.1 provides the combined five-level list for all EA-PDF. Current rules reproduce the normative list correctly but cannot alone reveal that disagreement. The exact dated normative dependency is ISO/DIS19005-4:2024, not an unspecified PDF/A-4 edition. Record the chosen authority/edition and the Table2 conflict alongside #3/#4. Do not newly reject c/ci-4e solely on this finding. Existing T2-* registry records already acknowledge the conflict and user-authorized local edition policy.
Severity: high impact ambiguity; high confidence in inconsistency, no claim a particular unclarified resolution is authoritative.

5. Core-field Table4 is not the same contract as XMP Table18.
Rules affected: MESSAGE_SENT_XMP #178, MESSAGE_RAW_SENT_OMIT_IF_VALID #181, MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT_XMP #187 and missing canonical email Content-Type counterpart.
Source: §7.3.1 Table4 printed p37; normative Table18 pp86–88 (metadata reviewer owns detailed comparison).
Table4 allows Sent to be blank, calls Raw-Sent optional when a valid date exists, lists Content-Type as always required, and calls attachment count always required. Current normative rule summaries respectively require typed Sent, recommend omitting unnecessary Raw-Sent, and make count required only when nonzero. Table4 differences must be documented, not silently enforced as additional XMP properties. Current registry already retains T4-* differences, but current rule catalogue alone does not explain them.
Severity: high impact ambiguity for drafts/corrupt emails; high confidence that Table4 differs. Coordinate final classification with metadata reviewer.

6. Collection Size remains unresolved, while Message-ID is a straightforward Table6 addition.
Rules: COLLECTION_SCHEMA_FIELD #16, COLLECTION_SCHEMA_PRESENT #86.
Source: §7.6 Table5 p53; §9.5 Table6 p68; ISO32000 Collection Schema Size subtype.
Table5 says original-message bytes; Table6 prescribes the built-in Size subtype, which reports embedded-file bytes. One PDF may contain many messages, making the distinction substantial. Current #16/#86 already explicitly acknowledge this; retain it as an unresolved source issue, not an unfixed historical defect. Table5 lacking Message-ID is not sufficient to omit it: normative Table6 expressly requires that schema field.
Severity: medium unresolved semantics; high confidence.

7. Useful creator guidance is represented in the secondary registry but absent from numbered executable rule text.
References: preprocessing provenance §7.2 p34; meaningful filespec Desc §7.2 p35, §7.5 p44, §7.7.3 p57; exact binary attachment deduplication §7.1.3 p33; zero-length placeholder policy §7.5 p44; matching visible page numbers and PDF PageLabels §7.4.1 pp39–40; Image XObjects for converted image assets §7.4.2.1 p41; font/resource reuse §7.4.3 p42; useful/collapsed outline hierarchy §7.7.2 p57.
Closest rules: #8 (source); #10 PAGE_CONTEXT_PRESENT_RECOMMENDED; #12 ANNOTATION_CONTENTS_REQUIRED; #53/#54 outlines; #63/#64 referenced assets. Several have no rule number. The current view-only registry tracks them under SOURCE-PROVENANCE, FILESPEC-DESCRIPTION, EMBEDDED-DEDUP, ATTACHMENT-ZERO, PAGE-LABELS, IMAGE-XOBJECTS, FONT-REUSE and OUTLINE-HIERARCHY. Since creator and validators are said to be based on validator_rule_text.json, make the absence/ownership explicit. These are primarily creator checks or recommendations, not grounds to manufacture new mandatory file failures. Desc is specifically inconsistent in strength ('ought' versus 'need') and needs an explicit interpretation rather than an undocumented hard fail.
Severity: low/medium completeness and maintainability gap; high confidence. Already catalogued outside executable rules.

Correct interpretations to preserve
- SOURCE_IN_ISOLATED #1 correctly distinguishes isolated provenance from a prohibition on every Source association. Object-level Source assets remain allowed (§3.1 p7; §7.4.2.1 pp40–41).
- Exact original source means unmodified bytes (§5 p18; §7.2 p34), BUT §7.2 pp34–35 expressly permits exporting individual messages to EML or combining sources BEFORE converting. An exported EML can be the conversion source of an s file. Do not equate valid EA-PDF conversion with proof of complete preservation of the originating PST/MBOX; provenance and scope must be stated. Do not declare every derivative export necessarily isolated.
- Embedded source assets may contain additional unrendered messages, contacts or calendar data (§7.2 pp34–35). #8 already allows this.
- Source fidelity cannot generally be proved by internal PDF/XMP consistency alone (§6 p22, §9 p61). Current evidence limits are generally appropriate.
- It is not mandatory to retrieve or separately retain every remotely referenced asset (§7.4.2.1 pp40–41). #63/#64 correctly say SHOULD when individually preserved.
- Extra/missing native attachment bytes are governed by source/policy evidence; zero-byte placeholders and separate PDF/A Alternative renderings are expressly supported (§7.5 pp44–48). An Alternative is not the native payload.
- Collection folders are optional; empty folders and nested containers are permitted (§7.6 pp51–52). Do not reject them based on navigation advice. Apart from original source assets, actual collection members must be EA-PDF (§7.6 p54); ordinary PDF/A attachment alternatives inside child mail files remain a different location/use.
- Collection Size conflict is already acknowledged by #16/#86, Collection key typo is corrected by #77/#78, optional View is correctly handled by #82, and no blanket original-source ban remains in #1.
- #58's SHOULD for source text correctly follows normative §9.3 p64 despite earlier §7.4.1 p39 'must' wording. #61's SHOULD for sRGB similarly follows normative §9.3 p65. Do not restore historical over-strictness from descriptive prose.
- #90–#95 preserve Table7's required GUID, optional Message-ID, and profile cardinalities, including no such identifiers on ANY c/ci DPM node. No new Table7 issue found in this limited cross-check.

Clause coverage
§1 scope; §2 terms/normative strength; §3 and §§3.1–3.2 all six profiles and Tables1–2; §4 all reference/dependency descriptions; §5 definitions; §6 scope; §7.1 and §§7.1.1–7.1.4 metadata/content sets/embedded files/URLs incl Table3; §7.2 source preservation; §§7.3.1–7.3.2 core/other headers incl Table4; §§7.4.1–7.4.4 body rendering/referenced assets/plain text/URLs; §7.5 and §7.5.1 attachments/example; §7.6 structured containers incl Table5; §§7.7.1–7.7.3 navigation; §7.8 modification workflows. Cross-read normative §9.1–§9.6 through Table7 to resolve severity and wording conflicts. Every assigned early clause read directly. No unreviewed early subsection remains.

structure.review_note:
EA-PDF current-rule audit: clauses 8 through 9.7
Read-only review, 2026-10-31. Source docs/reference/EA-PDF-v1.pdf; current validator_rule_text.json, 213 rules. Read all assigned normative text and Tables 6-13 directly. Visually checked printed pp74-75 (physical pp81-82) to verify role-map directions and Table10 trigger. No product files changed; runtime behavior not generally tested.

CURRENT TEXT THAT NEEDS WORK

1. MIME parameter rule omits mandatory presence/type/source condition.
Rule 69 SOURCE_MEDIATYPE_PARAMETERS_MATCH; section9.4 p66.
The source requires that when an embedded file originates from email that specifies MIME parameters, those same parameters SHALL be supplied in Mail_MediaTypeParameters as a PDF string. Current prose only requires agreement with associated XMP parameters. These are different assertions: PDF/XMP mutual agreement does not prove that required original parameters exist or have the prescribed PDF type.
Correction: retain conditional existence, PDF-string type and original-parameter preservation explicitly, followed by the separately testable XMP comparison. Lack of original evidence can leave source preservation unverified; it should not erase checks supportable from the PDF.
Confidence: high. Current extraction gap; no claim that all corresponding code checks are absent.

2. DPM ownership requirement has been reduced to identifier membership.
Rules90 DPM_MAIL_GUID_PRESENT,91 DPM_MAIL_GUID_MATCH,92 DPM_MAIL_MESSAGEID_MATCH; section9.6 p69 and Table7p70.
The specification requires intermediate email nodes to associate each email with ALL of that email's Content Sets. The separate inventory DPM-EMAIL-OWNERSHIP correctly records this but maps to rules90-92. Rule90 says ownership is a separate assertion without stating it;91 matches identifiers against document-global XMP;92 checks corresponding identifier. Rule135 custom structure ownership does not replace DPM ownership because custom tagging is optional.
Correction: explicitly preserve the all-content-set ownership obligation and give its evidence/check a distinct mapping. A GUID appearing somewhere in document metadata is not enough to prove correct ownership.
Confidence: high for current text incompleteness; runtime completeness not established by this read-only audit.

3. Annotation wording loses the precise geometry requirement.
Rule59 ATTACHMENT_ANNOTATIONS_PRESENT; section9.3p65.
Source: each attachment listed in document-level XMP must have an attachment annotation entirely inside the page CropBox within each email-body Content Set. Current prose retains per-body-set scope and visibility but not 'entirely within CropBox'.
Correction: name complete CropBox containment explicitly, separately from payload association and each-body-set occurrence. Visible does not mean fully inside the CropBox.
Confidence: high. Root also independently confirmed this candidate.

4. Recommendations still sound mandatory in concise runtime prose.
Rules74 EMBEDDED_SIZE,75 EMBEDDED_MD5,76 EMBEDDED_MD5_BINARY_FORMAT:9.4p67.
Rules105 CUSTOM_CONTENTSETS_TAGGEDPDF_RECOMMENDED:9.7p74;124 HEADER_FIELDS_TAGGED_RECOMMENDED:9.7p76;144/146/148 *_NESTING_RECOMMENDED:Table13p79.
The specification says SHOULD; current text uses imperative Add/Create/Tag/Nest. Rule74 mentions optional presence;75/76 do not. Separate inventory strength metadata does not make the standalone rule text clear.
Correction: say 'Writers should...' for optional checksum/size, tagging and ancestry; distinguish optional entry presence from mandatory type/correctness when supplied. In particular76 should concern supplied CheckSum values, not imply adding the field is mandatory. Retain real mandatory FieldValue/immediate-parent constraints from122 separately.
Confidence: high. Existing 2026-10-27 report Finding43 intended this cleanup, but these current entries retain the ambiguity.

5. Table10 used-only role mapping is an additional unlabelled interpretation.
Rules109 ROLEMAP_MAIL_TAGS and112-117 MAIL_*_ROLEMAP_*; section9.7p75Table10.
Printed text says if ANY listed custom element occurs, 'the following role map SHALL be included', followed by the complete six-entry table. Current112-117 instead trigger each mapping only when that individual tag is used; Python check_logical_structure and later detailed checks likewise skip unused mappings. The existing SPEC-ROLEMAPNS-SCOPE local resolution explicitly covers Table9 used-only mappings and unused namespace handling, not Table10.
Correction: preserve literal full-table trigger alongside an explicit project decision to require only used mappings, or request authoritative clarification. Do not silently impose stricter full-table behavior merely from this audit: intended scope is ambiguous.
Confidence: high that literal trigger and extracted trigger differ; medium about intended specification meaning. This is a traceability/interpretation issue, not proven code nonconformance.

6. Attachment-rendering source media types remain a bounded coverage gap.
Rules101 DPM_SUBTYPE_REQUIRED,102 DPM_SUBTYPE_MEDIA_TYPE_NAME,103 DPM_BODY_MEDIA_TYPE_MATCH_SOURCE; Table8pp70-71.
Table8 requires both BodyRendering and AttachmentRendering source media type/parameters. Current103 truthfully covers bodies only. InventoryT8-SUBTYPE includes both but its broad mapping must not be taken as proof of attachment fidelity.
Correction: split required-presence, PDF-name/MIME syntax, body-source match, and attachment-source match as separate obligation fragments with explicit evidence status. No requirement to invent associations where original evidence is absent.
Confidence: high. ALREADY ACKNOWLEDGED 2026-10-27 Finding45 and current103; remaining work is executable/traceable coverage, not a newly discovered extraction mistake.

REMAINING SOURCE AMBIGUITIES ALREADY GIVEN LOCAL DECISIONS
These are not new code defects and should not be presented as unresolved implementation tasks simply because official errata are absent:
- #44 PROFILE_NFSM_CONTAINER,9.1p62: literal c/ci UseAttachments versus PDF1.7 value availability. Current local UseOutlines for1.7 explicitly labelled; parent confirms ISO Table147.
- #51 CONTENT_SET_NONBLANK,9.2p63: current at least one nonblank page per set, blank additional pages allowed, explicitly local.
- #70 EMBEDDED_MEDIATYPE_RECONSTRUCTION,9.4pp66-67: published algorithm appends semicolon even without parameters; project conditional semicolon explicitly local.
- #107 ROLEMAPNS_PRESENT and#109 ROLEMAP_MAIL_TAGS,9.7pp74-75: optional custom tags versus broad PDF/A4 namespace/map language, used-only Table9 scope; existing dated local decision.
- #120 MAIL_CONTENTSET_CHILDREN,Table11p76: undefined Mail_ContentField changed locally/user-approved2026-10-19 to Mail_Field. Preserve literal spelling in source evidence; no need to re-fix current text.
- #140 MAIL_CONTENTSET_NESTED_UNDER_MESSAGE,Table13p79: all sets below Mail_Message conflicts with c/ci ban and document-wide sets; extended document-wide exception already implemented2026-10-27. Do not revert.
- #16/#86 collection Size field conflict between Tables5 and6 remains explicitly documented; parent/other agent handles7.6.
- #77/#78 correctly use actual PDF key Collection rather than specification typo Collections.
- #80 correctly requires ADBE ExtensionLevel exactly5 forPDF1.7; do not relax to>=5 from unresolved discussion.

VERIFIED DETAIL: Table9 first mapping is Artifact -> Private, not the reversed mapping quoted in some upstream discussion. Visually verified printedp74, physicalp81. Current109 is correct. Table10 exact direction Mail_Message->Document,Mail_ContentGroup->Part,Mail_ContentSet->Art; field mappings are writer-chosen suitablePDF1.7tags.

DELEGATION/REGISTRY COMPLETENESS (root investigating)
Section9.4p66 explicitly requires every embedded stream's Subtype and prohibits semicolons/parameters inside it. EMBEDDED_SUBTYPE_PRESENT and EMBEDDED_SUBTYPE_NO_PARAMETERS are retired from current213-ruleJSON and delegated upstream; requirements.json retains EMBEDDED-SUBTYPE-PARAMS with no active candidate. This need not be missing executable validation if external coverage is proved, but the runtime JSON alone is not a full extracted normative specification. Retain obligations in authoritative inventory with exact upstream rule/profile mappings rather than deleting their normative existence. Root auditing profile coverage.

Section8 is conforming SOFTWARE behavior, not staticPDF conditions. Its rendering/extraction/security/user-interaction requirements must remain separately inventoried and out of file failure decisions. No viewer development is requested. Published examples6/7 contain malformed references/objects and inconsistent tag examples; they should not override normative text/tables or become positive compliance fixtures merely because they appear in the specification.

metadata.review_note:
Independent metadata audit — current rules, 2026-10-31
Scope: §9.8, Tables 14–19, and §7.3.1/Table 4. Read original extracted text in full, then visually checked Table 4 (printed p37) and Table 18 (printed pp87–88). Compared current validator_rule_text.json/rules.txt, requirements.md, and the final working decisions in specification-reexamination-2026-10-27.txt. No product files changed.

Main conclusion
The current metadata rules contain substantial corrections already made on 27 October. I did not find evidence for declaring the whole metadata extraction wrong. Remaining work principally concerns source-dependent obligations disappearing from runtime descriptions/mappings, proof coverage, and unresolved source ambiguities. Do not report already corrected historical wording as current defects.

CURRENT EXTRACTION/TRACEABILITY WORK

M1. Explicitly carry the all-nonempty-fields obligation through to its check.
Source: §9.8.3, printed p86; §7.3.1, printed p36.
Current rules: 171 EMAIL_XMP_CONTAINER; 172/173 MESSAGE_TO_XMP/FOAF; 175/176 MESSAGE_FROM_XMP/FOAF; 182 MESSAGE_SUBJECT_XMP; 183 MESSAGE_ID_XMP; 188/189 MESSAGE_CC_XMP/FOAF; 191/192 MESSAGE_BCC_XMP/FOAF; 194 MESSAGE_INREPLYTO_XMP. Also 8 MESSAGE_SOURCE_MATCH.
Current inventory XMP-EMAILS correctly says SHALL record all nonempty Core Fields but maps only to rule171. Rule171 now describes unordered containers and Table18 schema, saying source completeness is distinct, without actually stating the nonempty-source inclusion obligation. The per-field texts call fields optional and refer to an unnamed separate source-dependent check. HEADER-SOURCE-EQUIVALENCE is mapped to rule8, whose current text says original assets cover represented emails, rather than requiring fidelity of their Core Field values. The source obligations survive in the review inventory but are not clearly preserved in the mapped runtime descriptions.
Needed: explicitly distinguish (a) internal container/property/type validity, (b) required inclusion when the original contains a nonempty field, and (c) equivalent original values subject to legitimate encoding differences. Link each to its actual check/evidence. Missing original evidence means unverified comparison; it must not redefine a preservation obligation as optional. Avoid treating raw-address helper fields as universally mandatory just because normal addresses exist: the Table18 Raw-* properties remain optional except the specific Raw-Sent condition.
Confidence: high as text/mapping issue. This audit does NOT prove that code omits all such comparisons.

M2. Preserve semantic coverage gaps explicitly instead of counting an ID mapping as complete.
Source: §9.8.2/Table16, printed p85.
Current rule167 ASSET_NUMBERMESSAGES_TYPE honestly says it checks only a nonnegative integer, not whether that many messages were successfully rendered from that particular asset. The inventory T16-NumberMessages still combines type and count semantics and maps only to167. This is already acknowledged in the 27 October final decisions, so it is outstanding work, not a new defect.
Needed: split type proof from successfully-rendered-count proof, identify what trustworthy source-to-message mapping establishes the latter, and report unavailable evidence explicitly. Counting all input messages, all PDF emails, outlines, or all attachment records is not equivalent.
Confidence: high; present rule wording itself confirms the gap.

M3. Make inherited XMP-extension duties visible in the complete rule catalog.
Source: §9.8.1, printed p84: PDF/A-3 EA-PDF must include an EA-PDF XMP extension schema according to PDF/A-3 §6.6.2.3.2.
There is no active rule mentioning this full obligation, but root confirmed a retired PDFA3_EAPDF_XMP_EXTENSION_SCHEMA inventory entry and static mapping to pinned upstream PDF/A schema/property checks. This is intentional delegation, not evidence of absent enforcement.
Needed: an authoritative complete-source catalog should show this obligation, its PDF/A-3-only applicability, delegated profile/rule IDs, and actual execution evidence. Do not invent a duplicate custom runtime check merely to fill the active 213-rule list.
Confidence: high on text/delegation distinction; runtime execution is outside this subaudit.

M4. Explain which part each duplicate or bundled text proves.
Examples: 165 SOURCE_MIME_TYPE and166 ASSET_CONTENTTYPE have identical descriptions;168 ASSET_CHECKSUM_FORM and169 ASSET_MD5_MATCH have identical descriptions despite format versus byte-digest proof being different;184 MAIL_GUID_XMP and185 MAIL_GUID_UNIQUE likewise; fourteen/source attachment record duties are combined under14 ATTACHMENT_XMP_MATCH. This is not in itself an incorrect requirement, but makes a rule count or mapped-ID count unsuitable as completeness proof.
Needed: atomic source requirements with separate mandatoryness/applicability, representation, ownership, value comparison, and unavailable-evidence outcome; retain stable runtime codes if compatibility requires them.
Confidence: high on duplication; priority lower than missing source linkage.

UNRESOLVED SPECIFICATION QUESTIONS, ALREADY LOCALLY DECIDED

S1. Sent on a blank or unusable original.
Table4 p37 says Sent is required even if blank; Table18 p87 requires xsd:dateTime, which cannot be blank. Rules178 MESSAGE_SENT_XMP and179 MESSAGE_SENT_FORMAT follow Table18. 27 October policy keeps Sent required and rejects creation if no honest date can be recovered; it does not substitute conversion time. Source needs an explicit unknown-date representation and normalization/substitution provenance. This is an unresolved source conflict, NOT a fresh finding that current rules wrongly make Sent optional. Sent is correctly required now. High confidence.

S2. Email Content-Type missing from Table18.
Table4 p37 requires email Content-Type even if blank, but Table18 pp86–88 does not define it. Current T4-Content-Type is creator guidance, with no corresponding mandatory email XMP field. 27 October decision explicitly avoids inventing that field. Body DPM media types and attachment Content-Type do not substitute for an email's original top-level multipart type. Source correction remains needed. High confidence.

S3. Message size/count requiredness.
Table4 p37 calls original message size and attachment count required. Table18 p88 makes SizeInBytes optional and NumberAttachments required only for one or more attachments, default zero. Rules186 MESSAGE_SIZE_XMP and187 MESSAGE_ATTACHMENT_COUNT_XMP deliberately follow Table18. The local decision should remain linked from the rules; do not call it an unrecognized extraction error. High confidence.

S4. Raw-Sent when the original date is valid.
Table4 p37 permits it optionally; Table18 p87 says it SHOULD NOT be present. Rules180/181 correctly preserve Table18's required-if-invalid/recommendation-if-valid distinction. The exact recommendation differs between tables but neither forbids a valid-date Raw-Sent outright. Do not turn SHOULD NOT into a mandatory failure. High confidence.

S5. Unspecified/ambiguous serialization.
§9.8.3 p86 describes an unordered set but does not name the outer email-list property. Rule171 does not make the established local pdfmailmeta:email choice explicit. Table18 p88 calls In-Reply-To an 'unordered sequence'; rule194 explicitly and honestly chooses rdf:Bag locally. FOAF Agent/address URI/raw malformed-address representations need authoritative examples. All were recognized in final27October decisions; retain explicit local-policy labels. High confidence.

S6. Attachment ownership and record-to-stream binding.
Table19 pp89–90 allows Message-ID-only ownership and does not require a unique per-attachment stream link. Duplicate Message-IDs, repeated names, shared streams, and optional checksums can leave unresolved identities. Rules14/59/199 contain cautious local matching policy; the source itself does not fully specify that algorithm or conflicting-identifier precedence. Do not strengthen conditional Mail_GUID presence to universally mandatory or accept another email's bytes as evidence. Already recorded local decision; high confidence.

S7. Malformed original attachment media type versus embedded stream type.
Table19 p90 demands preservation of original errors, while other stream rules demand valid reconstructed media typing/equivalence. Rules200/201 now correctly preserve malformed original text and do not simply require IANA syntax for the raw field. The source still needs a complete conflict policy when both demands cannot simultaneously hold. Already documented; high confidence.

S8. Creation-date event and creator attribution.
§9.8 p84 explicitly names the EA-PDF creation date; upstream issue22 has disagreement, not an adopted normative correction. Rule156 labels the PDF-creation-event interpretation local;157 separates historical proof. Rules152–155 correctly avoid guessing creator/producer validity from whether a value looks human, like an email, or like a product. Keep date debate and provenance proof separate from valid XMP Date syntax. Root handles current issue details. High confidence.

CORRECT CURRENT DETAILS — DO NOT REOPEN AS ERRORS
- Table14 namespaces/prefixes are correctly preserved; split-line meta/ URI is one URI, not two.
- version1, rev2024, lowercase conformance with i last are correct.
- Table16 original-asset ContentType/Checksum are case-sensitive spellings different from Table19 Content-Type/CheckSum.
- Table17 common MIME examples are not a closed allowed-type list.
- Table18 Sent is required; NumberAttachments has the conditional presence rule.
- Table18 Mail_GUID does not impose a canonical UUID textual grammar; identifiers retain exact Unicode values.
- Table19 Message-ID is NOT completely unmapped: current ATTACHMENT_XMP_MATCH maps T19-Message-ID.
- Table19 attachment SizeInBytes describes stored embedded bytes, allows permitted zero-byte placeholders; message SizeInBytes describes original single-message source including encoded attachments.
- Optional attachment CheckSum, when supplied, has mandatory 32-ASCII-hex syntax; it is not universally required.
- §9.8.4 distinguishes SHOULD-complete original attachment inventory from SHALL unordered set of zero or more descriptions. Current rule195 requires an empty Bag even with no attachments as an explicitly recorded local decision. Do not present this as an unrecognized overstrict rule or convert recommended inventory completeness into a universal SHALL.
